partner account teams and risk leads to explain Monzo’s requirements, obtain supporting evidence, review agreed controls and drive actions through to completion.</li> <li>Review evidence critically, challenge incomplete or unclear responses and decline proposed issue closure where the agreed standard has not been met.</li> <li>Agree routine actions, accountable owners and target dates with partner and internal teams, maintaining clear records and escalating barriers or material delays.</li> <li>Maintain the records and supporting evidence from standard operational checks completed during Global Ops partner visits, including practical observations of physical access, desktop security and local control execution.</li> <li>Travel periodically to partner locations and independently complete more detailed operational risk reviews, prioritised according to partner criticality, incidents, control concerns and assurance findings.</li> <li>Ensure these reviews complement formal TPRM and support media activity.<br><br></li> </ul> <p><strong>🤩 We’d love to hear from you if…</strong><strong><br></strong></p> <ul> <li>You have a deep understanding of VAIB principles and the barriers vulnerable customers face, driven by a strong commitment to improving customer outcomes through meaningful external collaboration.</li> <li>You have proven experience managing external relationships, going beyond relationship-building to set clear objectives, build trust, and hold both internal and external stakeholders accountable for delivering measurable benefits.</li> <li>You have experience teams across Monzo.</li> <li>You have a strong grasp of due diligence and risk management, ensuring all external partnerships are supported by rigorous governance and robust, accurate documentation.</li> <li>You are a highly organised problem-solver capable of managing multiple competing priorities, confidently navigating challenging stakeholder conversations, and proactively course-correcting when partnerships fail to deliver their intended value.</li> </ul> <p><em>Not ticking every box? title: Revenue Cycle Manager
description: About Us We are fixing US healthcare by building an AI-native physical care platform, starting with home health. Home health is a $140B industry with less than $10B in EBITDA â 40% of revenue is spent on pure administrative waste. We automate this work with AI, creating a fundamentally different cost structure compared to incumbents. This lets us rapidly take market share by serving the 30% of patients who go untreated today. By reshaping the cost structure of this industry, we unlock its growth. We've built one of the best AI teams in the world (from Character AI, Scale, Palantir, Citadel, Jane Street) and paired them with a team of healthcare veterans to build a new type of healthcare company: one that delivers care at the speed of an AI company. Our physical care platform already operates with 30pp higher gross margins than traditional home health providers. With our AI advantage, we pay nurses more, remove their admin burden, and unlock the scale economics that have been missing from this fragmented industry. If we served this entire $140B market, instead of $10B in EBITDA, we'd drive $60B. We're starting with home health, then expanding to all delivered care. Our mission is "any care, any where" . Fundamentally, our incentives are aligned with America. Every dollar in revenue we make is two dollars taken out of the healthcare system. If we succeed, so does US healthcare. Role overview Weâre seeking a hands-on Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) Manager to lead and support a team of specialists in a home health environment. This manager will stay close to daily operations, monitor team performance, and respond quickly to questions and emerging issues to help the team meet its goals. The role focuses on accounts receivable (AR), helping the team move outstanding claims from follow-up to verified resolution. What Youâll Do Manage and support RCM specialists working across home health revenue cycle workflows. Track attendance and monitor individual and team performance against established KPIs and daily quotas. Review workflow boards throughout the day to spot backlogs, red flags, and specialists at risk of missing their end-of-day quotas. Respond promptly to specialist questions while balancing real-time workflow monitoring and other team needs. Identify process gaps and work with the team to resolve issues affecting daily performance. Apply your home health and Homecare Homebase (HCHB) knowledge to help specialists navigate workflows and resolve operational questions. Accounts receivable and collections Guide specialists and team leads in prioritizing assigned commercial, Medicare, and Medicare Advantage receivables, including aged balances, payer responses, rejections, denials, and upcoming filing or appeal deadlines. Oversee claim follow-up through resolution: verify claim status and payment, investigate collection barriers and underpayments, and guide appropriate corrections, reprocessing, reconsiderations, or appeals under payer-specific requirements. Review and respond to escalations when a specialist cannot determine the next action; surface recurring payer, workflow, or system issues to leadership and coordinate their resolution. Ensure claim activity, supporting evidence, next actions, and follow-up dates are documented accurately in the applicable AR workflow and HCHB. Partner with billing, payment posting, prior authorization, clinical, and other teams to resolve discrepancies, obtain documentation, and follow paid-but-not-posted claims through resolution. Review proposed write-offs for documented collection efforts and supporting evidence, and route them through the required approval and posting process. Quality and team development Review claim work for accurate denial interpretation, appropriate action, complete documentation, timely follow-up, and correct escalation; use findings to coach specialists and strengthen performance. Support onboarding, payer and system cross-training, and regular knowledge sharing. Identify patterns behind collection challenges and update SOPs or workflows to prevent repeat issues. Share frontline feedback on AR dashboards and automation with relevant teams to improve prioritization, visibility, and specialist workflows. Basic Qualifications Strong experience in home health revenue cycle operations. Familiarity with Homecare Homebase (HCHB). Experience managing RCM specialists, including tracking attendance and performance KPIs. Experience monitoring workflows throughout the day and identifying risks to daily productivity targets. Experience identifying collection challenges and implementing processes to resolve. Working knowledge of AR follow-up, denial investigation, appeals or reprocessing, and payer-specific filing requirements. Experience reviewing claim documentation and quality, escalating unresolved issues, and coordinating with billing or posting teams. Ability to respond promptly to team questions while managing multiple priorities. Ability to identify workflow or process gaps and help the team address them. Preferred Qualifications Experience managing distributed or offshore revenue cycle teams. Familiarity with commercial fee-for-service and Medicare or Medicare Advantage home health claims, including episodic/PDGM workflows. Experience with AR dashboards, clearinghouses, and payer portals such as Waystar and Availity. Experience using denial trends, quality reviews, or operational data to improve collections workflows and team training. What We Offer Competitive salary Comprehensive health insurance, dental, and commuter benefits 401(k) retirement plan with employer contribution Opportunity for growth in a fast-growing company Collaborative team valuing innovation and problem-solving Please mention the word **MAJESTY** and tag RMy40Mi4xNTcuMTM5 when applying to show you read the job post completely (#RMy40Mi4xNTcuMTM5). title: Senior Product Manager
description: About us At Pencil, we are driving innovation in advertising technology through our state-of-the-art SaaS product, which harnesses Agentic AI to redefine content creation. Our mission is to make AI the default in advertising without replacing creative people. To achieve this, we need to make sure that our technology isn't just in the hands of big brands - we need to try to help small businesses and creative individuals too. The role Workflows are how most of the creative on Pencil gets made. A workflow is a visual sequence of steps, covering inputs, generation, brand assets, scoring, branching logic and delivery, that a person builds once and runs again whenever the job repeats, on demand or on a schedule. This role owns that product and the connections that feed it, with one goal: more workflows built and run, by more people, across every customer. You will own Workflows and Integrations. That covers the workflow builder, templates, scheduling and run management, and the steps that workflows are built from. It also covers the platform's third-party connections outside media: digital asset management systems, file storage such as Google Drive, translation services, data services such as Foreplay, and more than a hundred other business tools. You will make those connections part of the workflow itself, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them. You will build them on a common framework, so that each new connection is quicker to ship than the last and client teams can build on it for individual clients. You will also own how workflows show up inside Scribble, our creative agent. Agents can already run as steps inside a workflow. The next step is for Scribble to find, build, change and run workflows on a person's behalf and report back as they run, and for a workflow to pause for a person's decision and act on it. You will work closely with the team that builds Scribble, and you will own the workflow experience it works through, so that a workflow behaves the same whether a person or an agent is driving it. When that works, building a workflow stops being a specialist job. Key responsibilities Own the charter for Workflows and Integrations: the durable problem, success metrics, and an explicit in and out scope list. Grow adoption across every customer, measured by the number of workflows built and run and the number of people building them. Make building a workflow simple enough for a marketer or creative to do without help, through templates, guided set-up and defaults that cover the common jobs. Own the workflow experience that Scribble works through, so that an agent can find, build, change and run a workflow with the same tools a person uses. Make human review part of the run: a workflow should pause for a person's decision, record it, and continue down the right path. Make runs dependable at volume, with scheduling, run management, failure handling and clear status, so that a team trusts a workflow to run unattended. Own third-party integrations outside media, from digital asset management and file storage to translation and data services, and make them built-in steps in a workflow, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them. Set the integration framework and standards that client teams build on when they connect a system for a single client. Work with customers to find the jobs they repeat every week and turn them into workflows and templates that others can reuse. Run the full lifecycle from discovery to post-launch review, with a written hypothesis before every ship and a review against it afterwards. Use product data and structured customer feedback to set priorities, working backwards from evidenced customer need. Partner closely with design on the builder experience, and with engineering on run reliability and the integration framework. Partner with the PMs who own Scribble, agents and the editor, and with the client teams who build on your framework. Your background You will have three to five years of product management experience, and you want to own a key product and take it to the next level. You might be a great fit if you can walk us through: A product you grew from a small group of power users to broad adoption, and what you changed to get there. Shipping a builder, automation or workflow tool, and what you learned about making something powerful easy to start with. Building integrations with third-party platforms or APIs: how you chose which to build, and how you kept them working. A time you built from validated customer need in a domain you had to go and learn. If your instinct is to start with a demo, this is not the role. A decision you changed because the data told you to. Fluent in qual and quant. Experience with AI agents or AI-assisted products is a plus. You'll Thrive Here If Youâ¦ Move Fast. You're comfortable making decisions with imperfect information, iterating quickly, and fixing things before they become fires; Stay Human. You care deeply about users and teammates, and design with empathy for real workflows; Act Like an Owner. You take responsibility for outcomes, not just outputs. You spot problems early and take initiative to fix them. Keep It Simple. You fight unnecessary complexity, design reusable patterns, and make hard things feel intuitive. Love to Surprise. You enjoy finding unexpected ways to delight users, especially in the last mile of polish and usability. KPIs & Success Measures We will measure success through outcomes and quality, not just output: Builder share (lead): percentage of monthly active users who build or edit a workflow. Target [TBD]%. Workflow adoption (lead): percentage of monthly active users who run a workflow. Target [TBD]%. Workflow run growth: month-on-month percentage growth in workflow runs. Target [TBD]%. First workflow conversion: percentage of new users who complete a successful run within their first [TBD] days. Share of generations through workflows: percentage of all generations produced by workflow runs. Agent and human collaboration: percentage of workflow runs built or started by Scribble. Connector adoption: percentage of active workspaces that use at least one third-party connection in a workflow each month. Target [TBD]%. Integration usage: percentage of workflow runs that start from, or deliver to, a third-party connection. Target [TBD]%. Reliability (hygiene bar): percentage of runs that complete without manual intervention, held at or above [TBD]%. Learning velocity (supporting): percentage of launches reviewed after release against their stated hypothesis. Target 100%. Benefits 25 days PTO plus public holidays, although we operate a Flexible Time Off scheme Health insurance / private medical cover Monthly stipend towards wellness, fitness, and learning and development Remote - work from anywhere in your home country Enhanced parental leave policies, whether you become a parent through birth, adoption or surrogacy Access to our Pencil office in The Shard, London for our UK employees Flexible working hours Deep Dive About Pencil Pencil uses AI to make ads. Our mission is to make marketing effective and effortless. We want to become the default way ads get made - because AI ads are 10x faster and cheaper to make, and 2x better performing, than making them without AI. We're called Pencil because we believe AI will be a tool for creative people, not a replacement - it may even be as fundamental a tool in the future as the pencil was in the past. Pencil was founded in 2018 with a team from Google, Facebook and Uber with backing from Sequoia and Entrepreneur First. We were acquired by The Brandtech Group in 2023 to pursue a shared vision of bringing GenAI to the Fortune 500. https://www.trypencil.com About The Brandtech Group The Brandtech Group's mission is to be the best company in the world at helping leading global brands drive growth by connecting content, data and media using technology. It was founded in June 2015 (as You & Mr Jones) by former Havas Global CEO David Jones, with a simple mission to help brands do their marketing better, faster and cheaper using technology. It was renamed The Brandtech Group in January 2022. Today it generates more than $1BN in revenue and is the largest global digital content partner for many of the world's biggest brands and companies, often using its unique in-housing model. It works with eight of the world's top 10 global advertisers and 49 of the world's top 100. Clients include Banco ItaÃº, Danone, Google, Intuit, LVMH, Microsoft, Morgan-Stanley, Netflix, Reckitt, Renault-Nissan, PayPal, TikTok, Uber and Unilever. In addition, the Group invests in cutting-edge technology companies relevant to and with potential in marketing and has been investing in the AI, AR and the metaverse space since 2015. The Group was the first external investor in Niantic (creators of PokÃ©mon Go), alongside investments in AI Foundation (AI digital twins, personalized AI, and deep-fake detection 2018), Automat (AI chatbots, 2016), Elsy (AI media planning, 2016), Jivox (dynamic automated content, 2016), Crossing Minds (deep learning AI recommendation system, 2017), CreativeX (AI-driven content optimization, 2022), Zappar (AR, 2017), Provenance (blockchain, 2022) and GGP (the world's largest gaming fund). The Group is one of the most prominent marketing industry voices on the prediction and movement to AI-driven marketing, including Generative AI. description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. This role defines how our communities grow and deliver value, building experiences that foster meaningful connections, sustained participation, and long-term engagement. Define the purpose, format, agenda, speakers, and follow-up, partnering with program operations and event teams on logistics and delivery.</li> <li>Design the full member experience, including automated journeys and cross-functional workflows with Lifecycle Marketing, Marketing Operations, and program teams. Connect invitations, onboarding, event follow-up, ongoing engagement, and reporting so SELF and other programs scale without losing personalization.</li> <li>Build SELF's annual programming and marketing calendar. Coordinate experiences with GitLab's broader campaigns, launches, field activities, and marketing priorities.</li> <li>Put AI to work in community marketing. Experiment with ways to automate workflows, understand member feedback, personalize content, and make better decisions. Apply human judgment, review outputs for quality, and handle member data responsibly.</li> <li>Partner with Sales and Customer Success to identify priority accounts and top customer champions. Build relevant paths for them to join and contribute to community programs as members, speakers, and peer leaders, with coordinated outreach and follow-up.</li> <li>Collaborate with internal executive teams and crossfunctional partners, as well as external community partners to seed growth and integrate across existing plans. </li> <li>Track, measure and iterate on membership growth, event participation and quality, activation, retention, satisfaction, priority-account engagement, and advocacy. </li> </ul> <h3><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Experience building or scaling communities, membership programs, or peer networks.</li> <li>Ability to turn strategy into a clear growth plan, annual programming and marketing calendar, and coordinated member journey.</li> <li>An understanding of how community, customer engagement, advocacy, and account growth reinforce one another.</li> <li>Experience partnering closely with sales teams to identify priority accounts and customer champions and engage them in relevant programs.</li> <li>Demonstrated experience planning and delivering both virtual and in-person events, including community events. Ability to connect audience selection, programming, speaker engagement, and follow-up to member value and measurable outcomes.</li> <li>Familiarity with lifecycle marketing, marketing automation, CRM systems, web analytics, or campaign measurement.</li> <li>Strong cross-functional collaboration and writing skills, with the ability to communicate a program's value to different audiences.</li> <li>Ability to use member research, event feedback, engagement data, and marketing results to make decisions and improve programs.</li> <li>Sound judgment and the ability to balance ownership of SELF with marketing support for other community programs, working with operational partners on delivery.</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the Team </strong></p> <p>The Growth Community Programs team supports GitLab’s growth flywheel, seeding tomorrow’s customers and activating today’s. We design the programs and motions that turn customer and community relationships into lasting member value, advocacy, pipeline and expansion.</p> <p> </p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. title: GTM, Strategic Planning
description: Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search — all deeply integrated and designed for growth. We're building the best developer platform to power the next generation of software companies, and our go-to-market team is scaling fast to match. We're looking for a lead in Go-To-Market Strategic Planning, to shape how Supabase's GTM engine runs. This is a high-leverage, high-ownership role that sits at the intersection of strategy, data, and execution. You'll work directly with Success, Sales, Marketing, Finance, Partnerships and Product to build the systems, processes, and insights that help our go-to-market teams move faster and smarter. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own the end-to-end GTM Strategic Planning, covering territory design, segmentation design, target planning and GTM capacity planning. - Build and maintain a single source of truth for planning data across HubSpot, BigQuery and Hex. - Translate company priorities into field actions through designing the planning strategy and seeing it through to execution. - Partner with Sales Leadership to design and iterate on coverage models, segmentation, and team structures that reflect how developers actually buy. - Define and track the metrics that matter, and surface insights that drive action, not just reporting. - Lead the Strategic Planning roadmap: guide and lead in tooling investments and evaluate new systems and processes against real business needs. - Work cross-functionally with talent acquisition, ensuring GTM and territory models stay aligned. - Collaborate with GTM Engineering on automations and data pipelines so that your strategy translates into working systems, not just slide decks. WE'LL EXPECT YOU TO - Operate with high ownership. You set your own agenda, escalate when needed, and don't wait to be asked. - Work asynchronously and document clearly. We're a globally distributed team and writing is how we think. - Bridge strategy and execution. From drafting segmentation approaches in Google Docs to using SQL to monitor its effectiveness. - Build for scale without over-engineering. Simple systems that work beat perfect systems that don't ship. - Stay close to the customer. Developers are our buyers, and understanding how they discover, adopt, and expand is core to everything you'll do. YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF YOU - Have 6+ years of experience in Revenue Operations, Strategy Consulting, GTM Strategy, or Sales Operations at a B2B SaaS or developer-tools company. - Are fluent in the GTM stack: HubSpot, BigQuery, and Hightouch. - Can write SQL comfortably and aren't afraid to get into the data yourself before asking an analyst. - Have experience designing or overhauling sales processes, forecasting cadences, or territory models in a high-growth environment. - Understand product-led growth motions: PLS, usage-based triggers, and how PLG data flows into commercial pipelines. - Thrive with autonomy and are energized by building things that didn't exist before you joined. - Communicate with clarity across Finance, Sales, Success, Partnerships, Engineering, and Marketing without losing nuance. WHAT WE OFFER - Fully Remote We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world. - ESOP Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together. - Tech Allowance Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work. - Health Benefits Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us. - Annual Off-Sites Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year. - Flexible Work We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when. - Professional Development Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth. ABOUT THE TEAM Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love. - ~400 team members - 60+ countries - 20+ languages spoken - Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F) - 540,000+ community members We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

title: AI Transformation Owner, CRO
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h4><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h4> <p>The AI Transformation Owner drives the end-to-end AI agenda for the field organization, translating emerging AI capabilities into concrete enablement roadmaps, field use cases, and org-level strategy. You will partner closely with product and engineering teams to pilot and scale AI solutions, own the operational transformation plan needed to embed AI into day-to-day field workflows, and establish the governance framework that keeps AI adoption safe, compliant, and aligned with company standards. This is a hands-on role for someone who can move from strategy to execution without heavy oversight.</p> <p>This role reports to the Vice President, Enablement & AI.</p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do</strong>  </p> <ul> <li><strong>AI Enablement Roadmap:</strong> Own and continuously evolve the roadmap for AI-driven enablement initiatives, prioritizing based on field impact, feasibility, and alignment with broader Enterprise AI team and strategy..</li> <li><strong>AI Field Use Cases:</strong> Identify, scope, and execute on high-value AI use cases for the field (e.g., deal support, prospecting, content generation, guided selling, skills, change management), working with stakeholders to define success criteria and measure impact.</li> <li><strong>AI Field Champions: </strong>build relationships with champions in the field organization to activate power-usage and drive peer-led adoption; track this adoption (e.g., usage, proficiency, behavior change) with our AI Ops Specialist and Enablement Analyst.</li> </ul> <ul> <li><strong>Ops Transformation Plan:</strong> Design and drive the operational plan that turns AI pilots into scaled, repeatable processes, coordinating across enablement, ops, and technical teams to remove execution bottlenecks.</li> <li><strong>AI Governance:</strong> Influence and lead governance standards for AI tool adoption in the field, including data usage, risk review, tool vetting, and alignment with company-wide AI policy.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You’ll Bring </strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Mid-Senior Experience:</strong> Several years of experience in enablement, sales operations, or a related GTM function, with a track record of owning initiatives end-to-end.</li> <li><strong>AI Solutions Experience:</strong> Direct experience evaluating, piloting, or deploying AI tools or solutions in a business context, with a solid technical understanding of how they work and where they add value. Act as the field's primary advocate for AI tools (e.g., AI-assisted prospecting, call intelligence, forecasting copilots, RFP/proposal generation).</li> <li><strong>Cross-Functional Fluency:</strong> Proven ability to work closely with product and engineering teams, translating field needs into technical requirements and vice versa.</li> <li><strong>Self-Sufficiency:</strong> Comfortable operating with significant autonomy — able to define scope, structure ambiguous problems, and drive work forward without needing detailed direction.</li> <li><strong>Organization & Execution:</strong> Strong project management instincts; able to manage multiple workstreams (roadmap, use cases, ops transformation, governance) in parallel without dropping details.</li> <li><strong>Innovative Mindset:</strong> A builder's orientation toward new technology — curious about what's possible, willing to experiment, and able to separate genuine opportunity from hype.</li> <li><strong>Enablement/Sales Background:</strong> Familiarity with field or sales enablement motions (onboarding, tool adoption, content, coaching) and how AI can realistically augment them.</li> <li><strong>GitLab Values Alignment:</strong> Ability to work in an all-remote, asynchronous environment, leaning heavily on transparency and collaboration as defined in the GitLab Handbook.</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p>The Enablement & AI function is part of the CRO organization. You'll also mentor and coach fellow team members, sharing knowledge and learnings to elevate team performance. In your first year at this level, you'll deepen executive-level customer relationships, continue building a healthy book of business, and demonstrate consistent top-tier performance while supporting the growth of your peers.</p> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Own and grow a book of commercial accounts in your primary territory across Queensland, focusing on organizations that can benefit from GitLab's AI-powered DevSecOps platform.</li> <li>Drive the full sales cycle with commercial customers by generating and qualifying pipeline through outbound prospecting, then leading discovery, negotiation, and close to create new ARR.</li> <li>Work with your key customers to drive adoption and consumption in new products.</li> <li>Meet or exceed quota by building strong, long-term customer relationships and acting as the primary point of contact for all commercial opportunities in your territory.</li> <li>Articulate the value of GitLab to commercial prospects and customers, clearly connecting our platform to their business outcomes, productivity goals, and security needs.</li> <li>Manage your territory by documenting buying criteria and processes, defining next steps and owners, and keeping opportunity information accurate and up to date. Create clear quarterly forecasts against your plan through regular pipeline and deal reviews.</li> <li>Collaborate closely with partners, Sales Development, Customer Success, Renewals, and Solutions Architects to drive new business, ensure adoption, and support expansion while minimizing churn and contraction.</li> <li>Represent GitLab in customer meetings and events by driving attendance and delivering compelling presentations, proposals, and reports that communicate value and outcomes. Contribute customer ideas to our public issue tracker and apply MEDPICC and Command of the Message on all opportunities.</li> <li>Mentor and coach fellow Commercial Account Executives, sharing sales strategies, customer insights, and lessons learned to help elevate team performance and contribute to team goal achievement.</li> <li>Regularly meet on-site with key customers to develop and strengthen executive-level relationships, ensuring GitLab is viewed as a strategic, long-term partner at the highest levels of the organization.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Ability to drive complex B2B software sales cycles and build trusted relationships with commercial and Commercialet customers, ideally in a Commercial Account Executive or similar role serving Commercialet customers.</li> <li>Ability to quickly learn and sell a complex SaaS or DevSecOps platform to commercial and Commercialet accounts, including identifying and breaking into new maintain and advocate for these standards through code review</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>3-5 years of professional experience in GTM analytics, data science, or a similar technical role</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous business problems into clear, measurable questions and communicate technical concepts effectively to non-technical stakeholders.</li> <li>Experience with experimentation and causal inference (A/B testing, power analysis, quasi-experimental methods) and with statistical and machine learning methods such as regression, classification, clustering, and survival analysis</li> <li>Deep, hands-on understanding of SQL in cloud data warehouses (like Snowflake SQL), including working with product usage and event data, and in business intelligence tools (Looker, Tableau, Hex, or similar)</li> <li>Experience using Python for statistical modeling, machine learning, and production data science. description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As Director, Analytics Engineering, you'll lead a team of 8 and report to the VP of Data & Insights. You set direction across the data organization, stay close enough to the work to guide technical decisions credibly, and partner with Data Engineering, Data Science, IT, and business leaders.<br>You will have three mandates:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Build trusted, AI-ready self-service.</strong> Deliver a semantic model that answers business questions correctly, with the telemetry, evals, and model flexibility to prove it and keep costs in check.</li> <li><strong>Set the strategy for how GitLab accesses data.</strong> Own the data models, BI tools, and AI access patterns (Claude, MCP servers, Slack agents) that put trusted data in everyone's hands.</li> <li><strong>Build data applications the whole company relies on.</strong> Ship production-grade apps that combine trusted data, APIs, and AI to answer questions dashboards can't.</li> </ol> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Build and own a trusted semantic model, with governed metrics and business definitions, that answers business questions consistently across every tool</li> <li>Build evals and ground-truth datasets that measure answer quality, and use them to drive improvements and catch regressions</li> <li>Instrument telemetry to see who uses the semantic model and AI tools, what they ask, and where they get stuck</li> <li>Build a model-selection harness so GitLab can route work across LLMs and stay flexible on cost and quality</li> <li>Own data modeling and curated datasets for self-service, with the ownership, data contracts, testing, and documentation that make them AI-ready</li> <li>Define the AI data access strategy: when to use BI, Claude, MCP servers, or Slack agents, with the governance and security to keep access trusted and reliable</li> <li>Own the enterprise BI and self-service tools strategy (e.g., Tableau, Omni), including evaluation, adoption, and cost</li> <li>Build self-service capabilities, such as Claude skills, documentation, and guided workflows, that help people find and use data on their own</li> <li>Build and own company-wide data applications, from Claude-built single-page apps to apps inside BI tools, that combine Snowflake data, API calls, AI-powered deep dives, and write-back to Postgres or Snowflake</li> <li>Set engineering standards for data apps (security, authentication, testing, deployment, and monitoring) so they're reliable at company scale</li> <li>Set a long-range roadmap tied to company strategy, and a lightweight operating model that balances urgent stakeholder needs with investment in reusable data products and tech-debt reduction</li> <li>Hire, coach, and retain a high-performing team of 8: build career paths, develop leaders, distribute ownership, and recognize great work</li> <li>Act as customer zero for GitLab and GitLab Duo in data workflows, sharing feedback with Product and Engineering</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>12+ years in analytics engineering, data engineering, or BI, including 5+ years leading teams and 2+ years managing managers or senior leads</li> <li>Deep expertise in data modeling and semantic layers (e.g., dbt Semantic Layer, Snowflake semantic views, LookML, Cube), and expert dbt, including testing and CI/CD across a multi-team project</li> <li>Hands-on experience building LLM-powered data access (text-to-SQL, agents, MCP servers), including evals and telemetry for answer quality, and advanced use of AI coding agents such as Claude Code</li> <li>Expert SQL and strong Snowflake experience; working knowledge of Python</li> <li>Strong data governance experience: data quality, lineage, certified datasets, and access controls (RBAC, row access and masking policies)</li> <li>Track record of leading cross-functional data initiatives from strategy through adoption and measurable business impact, including enterprise BI and self-service at scale</li> <li>Systems thinker who sees how models, pipelines, and architecture decisions connect, and designs for second-order effects</li> <li>Exceptional communicator who writes clear technical specs, sets a clear vision, makes trade-offs visible, and influences executives and peers across the company</li> <li>Pragmatic in ambiguity: makes sound decisions on emerging technology and ships the right next version rather than waiting for the ideal end state</li> <li>Able to use GitLab, thrive in an all-remote, asynchronous company, model GitLab's remote working competencies, and work in line with GitLab's values</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Nice to Have</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience with LLM routing or gateway tools and managing model costs</li> <li>Experience with Tableau, Omni, or a BI platform migration</li> <li>Experience with web app development (e.g., React, TypeScript) and Postgres</li> <li>Experience owning finance or revenue-critical data (e.g., ARR, consumption) where accuracy and auditability are non-negotiable</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the Team</strong></h2> to use GitLab, thrive in an all-remote, asynchronous company, model and coach GitLab's remote working competencies, and work in line with GitLab's values</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Nice to Rethink planning, forecasting, and reporting workflows, and use AI tools to make them faster, more accurate, and more insightful.</li> <li>Redesign FP&A processes, policies, and planning and reporting systems for efficiency and effectiveness, with AI in the center. title: Director of Engineering, Database Excellence
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As Director of Engineering, Database Excellence, you will lead the Database Excellence stage and report to the Vice President of Data Engineering, in our Engineering department. You will set the direction for the databases that support GitLab.com, self-managed GitLab, and GitLab Dedicated. Your organization owns the reliability, capacity, health, and sustainability of GitLab's application datastores, with PostgreSQL as the primary focus alongside Redis, OpenSearch, ClickHouse, and object storage.</p> <p>You will be accountable for database capacity and availability on GitLab.com. You will guide long-range platform decisions while partnering with Infrastructure, Product, Distribution, Support, Security, and FinOps. The work includes reducing infrastructure costs, improving data growth controls and saturation detection, standardizing database services, rebuilding the self-managed upgrade experience, and contributing to GitLab's company-wide datastore strategy, including Cells partitioning. Learn more in the<a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/data-engineering/database-excellence/"> Database Excellence handbook</a>.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Set direction and long-range plans for the database platform in line with company strategy.</li> <li>Own database capacity and availability outcomes for GitLab.com, and communicate database risk to senior leadership.</li> <li>Lead and coach three Engineering Managers and develop Staff-plus engineers into leaders.</li> <li>Drive cross-division technical decisions using data, partnering with Infrastructure, Product, Distribution, Support, Security, and FinOps.</li> <li>Partner with Product to prioritize database platform investments and make infrastructure tradeoffs in the context of product outcomes.</li> <li>Own the hiring plan, organization design, retention, and performance management for teams across regions.</li> <li>Set quarterly objectives and key results and engineering key performance indicators for the stage, and manage the database infrastructure budget with FinOps.</li> <li>Serve as an escalation point for database incidents, standardize effective processes, and keep the handbook current.</li> <li>Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience leading managers of managers, including coaching newer managers.</li> <li>Experience working hands-on with PostgreSQL at scale, including capacity planning, upgrades, replication, performance, and large production clusters.</li> <li>Experience using data to make strategic technical decisions and connect database platform investments and tradeoffs with product outcomes.</li> <li>Experience supporting software that customers run themselves, or working through the self-managed upgrade challenge.</li> <li>Experience leading backend engineering teams that own production infrastructure, applying site reliability engineering practices including service level objectives, on-call operations, incident management, cost management, and automation.</li> <li>Experience communicating clearly in writing in an asynchronous, handbook-first company.</li> <li>Experience leading globally distributed remote teams.</li> <li>Experience with Redis, ClickHouse, OpenSearch, object storage, Google Cloud Platform, Kubernetes, Terraform, Chef, managed database services, FinOps, AI-assisted engineering workflows, or platform and infrastructure organizations is a plus.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>Database Excellence includes Database Architecture, Database Automation, and Self Managed Database. Three Engineering Managers lead these teams, alongside an Operations Manager. Our teams work across the United States, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and India. Database Architecture provides datastore guidance, data growth controls, and the database review process. Database Automation builds PostgreSQL fleet automation, upgrades, provisioning, health monitoring, and an internal managed PostgreSQL offering. translate financial targets into engineering investments, headcount plans, and execution roadmaps.</li> <li>You lead with ownership, speed with quality, and a focus on customer outcomes.</li> </ul> strategic enterprise and public sector accounts. Today, these are separate stages with a human making the call at each handoff. leaders, and give customers a credible path for managing software delivery at scale.</p> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Own the strategy, three-year vision, and business outcomes for GitLab's Agentic Software Delivery section, with a clear point of view on how artificial intelligence is changing software delivery.</li> <li value="2">Lead and develop senior and principal product managers across Continuous Integration, Artifact Management, Continuous Deployment, and Observability, helping them grow as independent decision-makers.</li> <li value="3">Establish the frameworks, standards, and operating rhythm that support consistent, high-quality product decisions without unnecessary escalation.</li> <li value="4">Own section-level key performance indicators and adoption funnels, using the results to reallocate investment or stop work that isn't paying off.</li> <li value="5">Evaluate major strategic bets, partnerships, and build, buy, or partner decisions, and develop the business cases that support them.</li> <li value="6">Partner with Engineering leadership on platform investment, architectural direction, and trade-offs across the section, while connecting build, package, deploy, and monitor into one coherent customer experience.</li> <li value="7">Drive pricing, packaging, go-to-market strategy, migration, and adoption with Product Marketing, Sales, Pricing, Customer Success, and Solutions Engineering across free, commercial, and enterprise offerings.</li> <li value="8">Represent the section with GitLab's senior leadership, key enterprise customers, partners, and industry audiences, while modeling AI-native product management across discovery, synthesis, prototyping, roadmap exploration, and concept development.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Experience leading product managers, including developing senior and principal talent, hiring, and addressing performance directly.</li> <li value="2">A track record of owning a portfolio across multiple product areas and being accountable for adoption, retention, and revenue, not only roadmap delivery.</li> <li value="3">Product management depth in one or more relevant areas, such as continuous integration and continuous delivery pipelines, artifact or package management, release management, or observability.</li> <li value="4">Sound judgment about where to invest and where to stop, including experience making and defending build, buy, or partner decisions with a business case.</li> <li value="5">Technical fluency to work with engineers and architects on pipeline design, artifact workflows, deployment strategies, and observability signals such as logs, metrics, and traces.</li> <li value="6">Experience shaping pricing and packaging for technical products across free, commercial, and enterprise offerings.</li> <li value="7">Experience working with technical customers in developer tools, DevOps, or software delivery environments where engineers and engineering leaders are primary users.</li> <li value="8">Executive-level communication and influence.</li> <li value="9">Practical use of AI tools in product management workflows, along with a thoughtful view of how AI and agentic workflows are changing software delivery. We welcome candidates whose experience may come from different but transferable product and leadership paths.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The team brings together senior product leaders across GitLab's software delivery platform and works closely with Engineering, Design, and go-to-market partners so customers experience these capabilities as one connected system. The team helps customers manage today's delivery complexity while shaping how AI-powered and AI-native workflows influence the next generation of software delivery. You'll connect reliability, scalability, and operability with the commercial decisions that make these platforms sustainable businesses.</p> <p>Your scope spans both platforms, not a single feature roadmap. On GitLab.com, you'll guide growth through better customer isolation and additional cells, alongside rate limits, usage limits, and monetization. On GitLab Dedicated, you'll help scale it to hundreds of customers through automation, customer self-service, and closer alignment with GitLab's latest releases. You'll balance customer needs with operating costs and gross margin.</p> <p>This director-level role starts as an individual contributor. It's remote and open to candidates based in the United States or Canada, with no specific time zone preference.</p> <h2><strong>What You'll Do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Set the product strategy and roadmap across GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated, connecting platform capabilities to customer and business outcomes.</li> <li>Drive improvements in platform reliability, scalability, and operability, including better separation between customers and expansion of GitLab.com's cell-based architecture.</li> <li>Define GitLab.com's rate limits, usage limits, and related monetization approach.</li> <li>Scale GitLab Dedicated through maintenance-window automation and other operational improvements, while controlling costs and improving gross margin.</li> <li>Expand customer self-service through Switchboard, giving customers tools to monitor, observe, and operate their Dedicated tenants.</li> <li>Guide capabilities such as customer-initiated disaster recovery and geographic redundancy, and enable earlier access to beta features on GitLab Dedicated.</li> <li>Reduce the delay between GitLab releases and their availability on Dedicated.</li> <li>Own the business side of the portfolio as well as the technical product direction, developing profit and loss (P&L) ownership for both platforms and helping establish GitLab.com as a P&L business.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What You'll Bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience leading a product portfolio at director level or with comparable scope, setting direction across multiple related products rather than a single roadmap.</li> <li>Technical product experience with cloud platforms, infrastructure, or SaaS environments, including the tradeoffs involved in reliability, scalability, and operations.</li> <li>The ability to connect product decisions to commercial outcomes, including monetization, operating costs, and gross margin.</li> <li>Experience translating complex platform challenges into product priorities and working across teams to deliver them.</li> <li>The ability to lead through product direction and influence in a director-level individual contributor role.</li> </ul> <p>Direct ownership of a product P&L is particularly valuable. Experience in an organization actively adopting artificial intelligence (AI) would also be helpful.</p> <h2><strong>About the Team</strong></h2> <p>The SaaS platform portfolio brings together GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated. The work spans shared-platform growth, single-tenant operations, and the tools customers use to manage their environments. The challenge is to improve the customer experience and platform capabilities while building a scalable, financially sustainable operating model for each offering.</p> <p>At GitLab, our mission is simple: to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world. You'll own the outcomes of GitLab's social function — strategy, budget, team development, tooling, and results — and serve as GitLab's senior-most voice on social strategy with executive stakeholders.</p> <p>This is a player-coach role. optimization, and subscriber and watch-time growth.</li> <li>Partner with Growth Marketing on paid social, including briefing creative, aligning organic and paid on shared audiences and messaging, informing boosting and amplification decisions, and connecting paid performance back to organic strategy.</li> <li>Develop clear, audience-focused campaigns that support company, product, brand, and talent goals.</li> <li>Guide content planning and publishing across social channels while maintaining a consistent GitLab voice.</li> <li>Own the social media budget, tooling stack, and agency, freelance, and production partner relationships.</li> <li>Partner with teams across Marketing, Communications, Product, Sales, Talent Acquisition, and other functions to plan and deliver social improve content and inform broader marketing decisions.</li> <li>Lead the measurement framework for social — KPIs, dashboards, and reporting cadence — and report performance and learnings to marketing and executive leadership.</li> <li>Partner with DevRel on community engagement to help GitLab participate in relevant industry conversations with a clear, useful point of view.</li> <li>Build and run creator, influencer, and advocacy programs, including developer creators, GitLab community contributors, and team member advocacy.</li> <li>Own GitLab's employee advocacy program — grow participation across Marketing, Sales, Engineering, and Talent, equip team members with content worth sharing, and measure reach, engagement, and contribution to brand and talent goals. Partner with Communications and Talent Acquisition on enablement, and manage the advocacy platform and its adoption.</li> <li>Support executive and expert social presence, partnering with Communications to help GitLab leaders and technical experts show up credibly on social, including constructive conversations with C-suite executives about proposed content.</li> <li>Apply AI tools thoughtfully across the social workflow to help GitLab model what an AI-native marketing team looks like.</li> <li>Prepare for and guide responses to sensitive or fast-moving issues in partnership with the appropriate teams.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>10+ years in social media, including at least 5 years leading social strategy for a global brand at the senior manager level or above, and accountable for the function's results.</li> <li>Experience owning a social function end to end, including strategy, budget, headcount, tooling, and results as the accountable leader. </li> <li>Experience leading teams, agencies, and cross-functional programs, with clear ownership of and accountability for outcomes.</li> <li>Depth in YouTube strategy, including owning and growing a brand or business channel, and can speak to programming decisions, video formats, packaging, and the metrics that actually move a channel.</li> <li>Hands-on experience growing LinkedIn and X as primary channels, with judgment about what content, format, and cadence work on each.</li> <li>Experience with paid social programs and how organic and paid social reinforce each other, including creative for paid, audience strategy, and interpreting paid performance data.</li> <li>Experience connecting social media programs to broader brand, communications, product, or business priorities.</li> <li>Strong editorial judgment and the ability to turn complex topics into clear, engaging content.</li> <li>Fluency with short-form and long-form video as core social formats, including working with production partners and creators.</li> <li>Experience defining a measurement framework for social, including KPIs, dashboards, and reporting cadence, and presenting performance, learnings, and recommendations to executive leadership on a standing basis.</li> <li>Experience building or scaling an employee advocacy program, including driving adoption across multiple functions, sustaining participation beyond launch, and reporting attributed reach and business contribution</li> <li>Fluency with an enterprise social stack for publishing, listening, and advocacy. Ours is Sprout Social, Meltwater, and EveryoneSocial.</li> <li>Experience running social programs across multiple regions and languages, and judgment about what to localize versus centralize.</li> <li>Skill in managing multiple priorities and making sound decisions in fast-moving situations.</li> <li>A collaborative, inclusive approach and the ability to work effectively in a distributed, asynchronous environment.</li> <li>Passion about GitLab's mission and the future of software development, open source, artificial intelligence, and DevSecOps.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>This role is part of GitLab's Marketing organization and works across teams to present a clear, consistent company voice on social media. description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2>An overview of this role</h2> <p>As Engineering Manager, Architecture Engineering: Async, you'll lead a distributed group of Site Reliability Engineers and Backend Engineers. You'll support their development and balance production reliability with platform projects, including zero-downtime Redis upgrades, support for single-tenant and cell-based deployments, and the move from queue-based job orchestration to a durable workflow engine.</p> <h2>What you'll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Lead, hire, and grow a team of site reliability engineers and backend engineers, supporting career development, promotions, and onboarding.</li> <li value="2">Own reliability for the job processing and caching platforms, including service-level objectives, error budgets, alerting, and weekly operational reviews.</li> <li value="3">Manage capacity planning, support escalations, and incident follow-ups, balancing operational work with roadmap projects and rescoping work when deadlines can't be met.</li> <li value="4">Run the team's part of GitLab.com's first-tier on-call rotation, including shift coverage, onboarding, and handovers, and serve as incident commander for high-severity incidents.</li> <li value="5">Drive zero-downtime Redis version upgrades and automate operating system patching and reboots.</li> <li value="6">Adapt job processing to run in single-tenant and cell-based deployments.</li> <li value="7">Own the migration from queue-based job orchestration to a durable workflow engine, defining the first use cases, a measurable migration path, and the roadmap.</li> <li value="8">Own quarterly planning and the team roadmap, and clarify shared operational responsibilities with partner teams, including Git storage.</li> <li value="8">Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.</li> </ul> <h2>What you'll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Experience managing an engineering team delivering high-performance services at scale, ideally site reliability engineers or infrastructure engineers running production software as a service systems.</li> <li value="2">Technical depth in background job processing and caching technologies such as Redis and Sidekiq, sufficient to guide decisions about upgrades, capacity, and failure modes.</li> <li value="3">Experience managing reliability against service-level objectives, including defining service-level indicators, setting up burn-rate alerting, and planning capacity.</li> <li value="4">Experience running a 24/7 on-call rotation and coordinating high-severity incidents.</li> <li value="5">A track record of balancing operational work and incident follow-ups with roadmap projects, and pushing back on scope when deadlines can't be met.</li> <li value="6">Experience leading a fully remote team across time zones in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia-Pacific.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The Async team runs GitLab.com's background processing layer, from the Sidekiq infrastructure to the shared code that enqueues jobs. Product teams build the jobs; we keep the platform that runs them fast and reliable. Our Redis clusters support caching, sessions, rate limiting, queues, and shared state. Your work will span renewals, overages and reconciliations, subscription visibility, and budget and reservation management, keeping subscription, billing, and account data accurate and reliable. Because these workflows directly affect revenue, customer access, and financial information, you'll use technical judgment, safe and iterative rollouts, and a high bar for reliability and correctness.</p> <p>Some examples of our projects:</p> <ul> <li value="1">Building a clear, reliable subscription view across the Customers Portal and related surfaces</li> <li value="2">Improving manual renewal and auto-renewal flows, including supporting emails, banners, and account experiences</li> </ul> <h2>What you'll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Design and build fullstack features across the post-purchase subscription journey.</li> <li value="2">Contribute to the technical design and implementation of new subscription lifecycle capabilities.</li> <li value="3">Partner with Product and Design to translate renewal, billing account, and customer experience requirements into resilient, well-tested solutions.</li> <li value="4">Integrate subscription lifecycle workflows safely with billing, customer account, and internal admin systems.</li> <li value="5">Write maintainable, well-tested code and follow engineering practices for rollout safety and monitoring.</li> <li value="6">Participate in code reviews and provide thoughtful, constructive feedback.</li> <li value="7">Identify and reduce technical debt and architectural risk in the subscription lifecycle.</li> <li value="8">Participate in incident response for subscription and renewal issues, given their potential impact on revenue and customer access.</li> <li value="8">Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.</li> </ul> <h2>What you'll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Professional experience as a fullstack engineer and confidence working across frontend and backend code.</li> <li value="1">Our purchase applications use Ruby on Rails (Must have) and Vue.js. (preferred) or React.</li> <li value="2">Experience owning technical direction for a product area, including proposing, discussing, and driving thorough, iterative solutions.</li> <li value="3">Experience building or maintaining transactional or checkout-style flows, ideally in a billing, ecommerce, or subscription context.</li> <li value="4">Familiarity integrating with third-party billing or customer relationship management systems, such as Zuora, Salesforce, or Stripe, is a plus, not a requirement.</li> <li value="5">A focus on safe, incremental delivery given the revenue and customer impact of this work.</li> <li value="6">The ability to communicate clearly and concisely about complex technical, architectural, and organizational problems and propose thorough, iterative solutions.</li> <li value="7">Written and spoken English proficiency sufficient to collaborate in a remote, largely asynchronous work environment.</li> <li value="8">Alignment with GitLab's values and a commitment to working in accordance with them.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The Subscription Lifecycle team is part of GitLab's Monetization section and owns the post-purchase subscription experience. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h4><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h4> <p>As a Lead Investor Relations team member at GitLab, you'll help rebuild our investor relations (IR) processes and shape how we communicate GitLab's strategy and performance to the public markets. Working closely with our VP of Finance Strategy & Operations, Chief Financial Officer (CFO), and executive team, you'll be a senior individual contributor with broad ownership of investor communications and relationships. You'll connect insights from across the business to explain our technical products, evolving business models, and long-term investment thesis.</p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do</strong>  </p> <ul> <li>Lead key workstreams of the quarterly earnings process, including messaging, scripts, questions and answers, data collection and synthesis, and conference call preparation; build repeatable processes with Finance, Legal, and executive leadership.</li> <li>Gather insights from research and development, Product, Sales, and other business leaders to explain GitLab's strategy, technical products, and business model transitions in investor communications and board materials.</li> <li>Own relationships with sell-side analysts and the investment community, monitor analyst models and consensus against our forecast, and flag gaps or risks to the head of IR and CFO.</li> <li>Prepare the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), CFO, and other executives for investor meetings, conferences, and roadshows; lead investor calls independently when executives aren't available, explaining how GitLab's business works and answering investor questions.</li> <li>Analyze peer and competitor earnings, Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings, and investor days; maintain benchmarking analyses and deliver quantitative and qualitative insights for executive and board discussions.</li> <li>Track GitLab's shareholder base and recommend investor targeting strategies to expand and maintain key ownership positions.</li> <li>Draft and review earnings decks, shareholder letters, fact sheets, and IR website content; partner with Finance, Legal, Communications, and Strategy to keep messaging consistent, accurate, and compliant with disclosure requirements, including Regulation Fair Disclosure (Regulation FD).</li> <li>Plan and deliver Investor Day with the head of IR to communicate GitLab's long-term story, alongside investor outreach, non-deal roadshows, and corporate access events.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You’ll Bring </strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience evaluating software businesses from a buy-side or sell-side investment perspective, gained through investing, equity research, investor relations, or a related field.</li> <li>Financial modeling, valuation, and quantitative analysis skills, with the ability to identify the business drivers that shape investor expectations.</li> <li>Experience producing or analyzing earnings materials and investor presentations, and explaining technical software products, evolving business models, and financial performance clearly in writing and conversation. You can work directly with senior executives and offer an informed point of view.</li> <li>Working knowledge of SEC reporting, Regulation FD, and public company disclosure practices.</li> <li>Proficiency with presentation and spreadsheet tools, experience with IR and market data platforms, and experience using artificial intelligence (AI) to improve workflows or a willingness to develop that capability.</li> <li>The ability to work independently and manage competing priorities in an all-remote, asynchronous-first environment, with an approach that reflects GitLab's values, especially transparency and efficiency.</li> <li>Nice to have: prior experience building an internal IR function.</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p>GitLab’s Investor Relations team drives the strategy and long-term market positioning of GitLab in the public financial markets. You'll join the Legal & Corporate Affairs (LACA) team as a senior individual contributor, reporting to the Senior Director, Associate General Counsel, Corporate & Compliance.</p> <p>You'll bring a strong securities law foundation and a broad corporate perspective to a small team. Your work will span quarterly reporting and earnings, the annual proxy statement and stockholders meeting, board and committee matters, equity plans, and subsidiary governance. You'll also support mergers and acquisitions (M&A) and other strategic initiatives. You'll work closely with Accounting, Corporate Development, Finance, Investor Relations, People, Product, Stock Administration, Tax, and Treasury. You'll translate complex legal issues into clear recommendations, build trust across functions, and balance legal risk with business objectives. </p> <p><strong>Location: </strong>This is a remote role open to candidates anywhere in the United States. We have a preference for candidates based in the San Francisco Bay Area, but we welcome applications from all US locations.</p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do</strong>  </p> <ul> <li>Own securities and public company reporting matters, working with internal stakeholders and external auditors on Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings, quarterly reports, earnings releases, the annual proxy statement, investor presentations, and other public disclosures.</li> <li>Advise on corporate governance, including board and committee processes, the annual stockholders meeting, corporate approvals, equity plan matters, executive compensation, and related compliance requirements.</li> <li>Provide legal guidance on complex entity matters across jurisdictions, including formation, maintenance, reorganizations, intercompany agreements, and wind-downs.</li> <li>Support M&A and other strategic transactions, contributing to diligence, documentation, approvals, signing, closing, and post-closing integration.</li> <li>Engage and manage outside counsel across jurisdictions, coordinating work and ensuring practical, high-quality, and cost-effective advice.</li> <li>Identify legal and business risks, present clear options to senior stakeholders, and monitor legal developments to keep policies, processes, and controls current.</li> <li>Build and improve playbooks, checklists, templates, and workflows for recurring corporate legal work. Train junior legal team members and cross-functional partners to use these resources.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You’ll Bring </strong></p> <ul> <li>6+ years of demonstrated relevant legal experience, including law firm experience advising US-listed public companies on securities law, corporate governance, and public company reporting. Prior in-house experience is a plus.</li> <li>A Juris Doctor (JD) degree and active admission to a US state bar.</li> <li>The ability to independently manage complex legal matters and cross-functional projects, prioritize competing needs, and drive work to completion with limited direction.</li> <li>Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain technical legal issues to non-lawyers and senior leaders and build trusted working relationships.</li> <li>The ability to investigate unfamiliar legal questions, weigh risks against business objectives, and turn recommendations into action.</li> <li>Experience improving legal processes, templates, policies, or other scalable resources.</li> <li>The ability to collaborate in a remote, globally distributed team across time zones and cultures, and willingness to use GitLab in your day-to-day work.</li> <li>Helpful but not required: in-house work at a public software-as-a-service (SaaS), software, or open core company; M&A; cross-border corporate matters; outside counsel management; or legal technology that helps scale legal work.</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p>The Corporate & Compliance team supports principled corporate governance and GitLab's culture of compliance. We work with leaders and subject matter experts across LACA and the broader company to provide practical, timely legal guidance. LACA is a globally distributed team that supports GitLab's growth through legal expertise, business partnership, and continuous process improvement. You’ll drive the reporting calendar, coordinate work across Accounting, Legal, Financial Planning and Analysis (FP&A), and Investor Relations, and improve the quality, clarity, and consistency of our disclosures and reporting processes. You’ll report to the Director of SEC Reporting and work remotely from the Americas.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Own the preparation, review, and filing of GitLab’s Securities package and review of financial information in the earnings release and script.</li> <li>Own the disclosure checklist and eXtensible Business Reporting Language (XBRL) review process, and identify ways to improve disclosure quality, clarity, and consistency.</li> <li>Improve the SEC reporting process by identifying inefficiencies, redundancies, and manual steps, then driving automation and standardization.</li> <li>Prepare or review journal entries, reconciliations, the equity rollforward, earnings per share calculations, and provided-by-client schedules for assigned areas such as stock-based compensation and stock repurchases.</li> <li>Ensure compliance with SEC and United States generally accepted accounting principles (U.S. GAAP) reporting requirements, research technical accounting issues, and lead the implementation of new accounting pronouncements that affect disclosures.</li> <li>Maintain Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) requirements for relevant areas, support internal and external reporting packages, and lead or contribute to special projects such as process improvements, new disclosure requirements, and merger and acquisition reporting.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>A bachelor’s degree in Accounting.</li> <li>Certified Public Accountant (CPA) licensure or active pursuit of licensure is preferred.</li> <li>Experience in owning SEC reporting deliverables, including Forms 10-K and 10-Q, in a public company or a public accounting environment serving public company clients.</li> <li>A record of improving disclosures and reporting processes, not only executing existing processes.</li> <li>Strong project management skills, with the ability to own a calendar, drive accountability across teams, and manage competing communication skills, with experience presenting to and influencing senior stakeholders and collaborating with Legal, FP&A, Investor Relations, and business partners.</li> <li>Proficiency with Workiva Wdesk and NetSuite is preferred.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>The Accounting team supports accurate, timely, and transparent financial reporting at GitLab. description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps.
